text:
maria.g: heads-up — support ticket from Acme: a bunch of 401s after our key rotation at 03:12 UTC. They see "invalid signature" and "kid not found" in our auth logs. Happening intermittently across their fleet.

tyler_h: ack. can you paste the raw error lines and which backend? region?

maria.g: logs from prod-west (svc-auth):
```
2026-03-14T03:15:22Z svc-auth ERROR validate_jwt: signature verification failed, token=<redacted>, err=invalid signature
2026-03-14T03:15:23Z svc-auth WARN jwks_lookup: kid=abc123 not found in jwks cache
2026-03-14T03:15:25Z svc-auth INFO jwks_fetch: fetched jwks from https://idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json, cache-control: public, max-age=3600
```
Also see a couple of `nbf`/`exp` rejects: `token not yet valid` for ~2% of requests.

oliver: do we have TTLs for jwks cache? max-age 3600 looks fine but rotation happened at 03:12 so maybe some nodes still had old key in memory. Are we honoring cache-control and also checking for kid mismatch?

maria.g: we store JWKS in an in-memory cache keyed by issuer; refresh is on schedule + on-evict. we only re-fetch when schedule triggers. current schedule is every 15m.

tyler_h: that sounds like the root cause: key rotated at 03:12, tokens issued immediately, some nodes waited up to 15m to refresh -> kid not found -> signature error. two-pronged problem: (1) eager validation fails instead of fetching new key on kid mismatch, (2) clock skew causing nbf/exp fails for a small percentage.

jamal: +1. quick mitigation: fallback fetch on kid mismatch. i.e., if kid not in local JWKS, do a background fetch of jwks_uri and retry validation (but be careful to rate-limit). Also add 5m leeway for exp/nbf checks.

maria.g: filed a quick patch: if kid not found -> synchronous fetch with 2s timeout, validate again; if still fails, return 401 and emit metric `jwt.kid_miss.refetch`. pushing to staging now.

oliver: for the clock skew, where are we applying leeway? I thought the validation lib had default 0s.

maria.g: yep, library default is strict. setting leeway to 300s (5m) reduces those rejects. not ideal long-term but good emergency band-aid.

tyler_h: do we have customers behind certain CDNs/proxies where time drift is common? might explain concentration.

maria.g: Acme uses some embedded IoT devices with poor NTP. they also do token caching.

sec-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0314-jenkins (automated note).

jamal: operational checklist I propose:
- rollback rotation? only if new tokens broken widely.
- invalidate service JWKS caches (push cache-bust event via config service).
- deploy kid-miss refetch patch to prod-asap in canary.
- increase JWT leeway to 300s temporarily.
- add metric and alert for `jwt.kid_miss.rate > 0.1%` and `jwt.signature.failures` spikes.
- run postmortem and update runbook.

oliver: we should also ensure we honor `Cache-Control` and `Expires` from identity provider. if they set `s-maxage` we should follow it for shared caches. and document that rotated keys might require immediate fetch on kid mismatch.

maria.g: added small code snippet to the PR for refetch behavior:
```
// pseudocode
try {
  validate(token, jwksCache[iss])
} catch (KidNotFound) {
  jwks = fetch(jwks_uri, timeout=2000)
  jwksCache[iss] = jwks
  validate(token, jwks)
}
```
Rate-limited to avoid thundering herd.

tyler_h: two more edge cases we saw in other customers: (1) `kid` missing from token header — some older clients strip kid and rely on implicit ordering; (2) alg mismatch where token `alg`=HS256 but server expects RS256 -> signature will fail. Need logging for both.

maria.g: added logging lines for missing `kid` and `alg` mismatches, and return 400 for `kid` missing with explanatory message linking to our troubleshooting doc.

jamal: communication plan: support to notify Acme that we're rolling a hotfix to service to aggressively refetch JWKS and to increase leeway. ask them to rotate tokens gradually and confirm devices have reasonable clock sync.

support-bot: Support ticket updated: #34721 — notified customer of workaround.

oliver: longer-term fixes:
- honor JWKS `cache-control` precisely and expose TTL metrics per issuer.
- proactive key rotation pre-notifications / publish rotation windows and rotate consumer-side keys gracefully.
- try fallback of retrieving single key by kid: some idps expose `jwks_uri?kid=...` — not standard but helpful.
- include a health endpoint for `jwks.cache_age_seconds` per issuer so ops can detect staleness.

maria.g: rolling to canary now. will monitor `jwt.kid_miss.refetch` and `jwt.signature.failures`. will post updates.

(5m later)

maria.g: canary deployed to 2/20 nodes — immediate drop in kid_miss errors for traffic routed to them. overall 401 rate went from 0.9% -> 0.12% for Acme. good sign.

tyler_h: great. plan to push to prod in 10m if no spike. also file follow-up to add per-issuer JWKS TTL dashboard.

jamal: postmortem owners? maria for incident runbook; oliver for JWKS cache refactor; tyler for alerts/dashboards.

maria.g: noted. also updating runbook with repro steps we used:
1) get a failing token sample from customer (they provided one).
2) on auth node run: `jwt_decode --jwks-cache /tmp/cache --token <token>` to reproduce locally.
3) run tcpdump to confirm which jwks_uri responded and cache headers.
4) if kid missing, ask for original client library version.

jamal: closing loop: please follow-up with engineering change request for immediate cache invalidation API and per-issuer TTL metrics.

maria.g: will do. marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if Acme still sees issues after 24h. :white_check_mark:
